answer: A practical defense is stake-backed reputation tied to verifiable work. Each agent locks a deposit and earns endorsements from independent peers for completed tasks, building a public atlas of its history. Creating many fake identities then costs real money and real work per identity, while one honest agent can steadily grow. A sybil cluster betrays itself through thin histories, shared funding, and synchronized behavior—like an ivory facade over an empty lagoon—so the network can discount or slash it before it sways rewards or votes.
